import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 277

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/277](https://www.erdosproblems.com/277)
- [Ha79] Haight, J. A., Covering systems of congruences, a negative result. Mathematika (1979),
  53--61.
-/

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos277

/--
Is it true that, for every $c$, there exists an $n$ such that $\sigma(n)>cn$ but there is no
covering system whose moduli all divide $n$?

This was answered affirmatively by Haight [Ha79].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_277 :
   answer(True) ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, ∃ n : ℕ, (σ 1 n : ℝ) > c * n ∧
      ∀ (m : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∃ i, (n : ℤ) ∉ m.moduli i  := by
  sorry

end Erdos277

reformulations.difference: The theorem uses integer ideals instead of numerical congruence moduli and states the unbounded-counterexample form of Haight’s negative answer to the sufficient-threshold question.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every nonzero proper ideal of ℤ is dℤ for a unique natural d ≥ 2. Injective moduli therefore mean distinct numerical moduli, the finite coset union means coverage of ℤ, and n ∈ dℤ means d ∣ n. Consequently, the final universal/existential clause says exactly that n is not a covering number. Also σ(0)=0 excludes zero witnesses, and for n>0 the inequality is equivalent to σ(n)/n>c. Negating Haight’s question—whether some c>0 forces every positive n with σ(n)/n>c to be a covering number—gives this assertion; allowing every real c is equivalent by using max(c,1). These equivalences were proved in the scratch file using an explicit finite distinct-modulus definition.

sources_consulted: J. A. Haight, “Covering systems of congruences, a negative result,” Mathematika 26 (1979), 53–61; full paper, especially pp. 53–54: https://static.cambridge.org/content/id/urn%3Acambridge.org%3Aid%3Aarticle%3AS0025579300009608/resource/name/S0025579300009608a.pdf?pub-status=live

Paul Balister, “Erdős Covering Systems,” Surveys in Combinatorics 2024 — summary and references: https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/surveys-in-combinatorics-2024/erdos-covering-systems/8C1FD7ABA25695B91DADC11251FB916D
